[folded GR-14.9.39.4-L2.1 = §14.9.39.4 2) a) 1.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work/PB459.md LANDED. FORMAT 1 GR2 a) 1 - arm a: 'If the value of arithmetic-expression-1 does not result in an integer' then EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT, the SET unsuccessful, the receiving operand unchanged; arm b: 'Otherwise, if the value of the arithmetic-expression-1 is outside the limit specified in General rule 2 of 13.18.38, OCCURS clause' then EC-RANGE-INDEX with the same two consequents; arm c: the ordinary store, 'even if that occurrence is not a valid occurrence within this table' (all cite.py --check 14.9.39.4 PASS). All three arms are now implemented in one place. EmitSetTo lands the sender through CobolIndex.TryAmount before any receiver is stored, so the statement is all-or-nothing as the rule states it. The guard rides every receiver kind and that is exactly right: 14.9.39.3 SR3 forbids arithmetic-expression-1 with an index-data-item receiver and SR4 requires index-name-2 with a numeric receiver (both cite.py-checked), so an arithmetic-expression sender implies every receiver is an index-name-1 - GR2 a)'s own population - while an index / index-data-item sender is a long occurrence number, integral and in range by construction, so the landing is a no-op on the GR2 b) and GR2 c) arms rather than a rule applied where the standard states none. MEASURED before, with '>>TURN EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT CHECKING ON' in force: 'SET IDX TO 1. SET IDX TO WS-F.' with WS-F PIC 9V9 VALUE 2.5 gave AFTER=[B] OCC=0002, the fraction truncated and stored, identical with checking off. MEASURED after: checking OFF gives TO-FRAC=+0000000000000000002 (unchanged); checking ON gives SUB=EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT then the same unchanged value. Arm c is pinned by NEGOCC=-0000000000000000003: SET IX TO -3 is legal and must not raise, which is what keeps the new guard from becoming a table-bounds test.

[folded GR-14.9.39.4-L2.2 = §14.9.39.4 2) a) 2.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work/PB459.md LANDED. FORMAT 1 GR2 a) 2 (identifier-2) plus the GR2 b) tail. Arm b - 'index-name-1 is set to a value causing it to refer to the table element that would correspond in occurrence number to the value of identifier-2' - was already implemented and measured correct. Arm a, the range consequent, is now closed, and the adjudication that left it PARTIAL rested on a premise this landing re-derived and corrected: the limit is the IMPLEMENTOR's index range (13.18.38.4 GR2, cite.py PASS), not the table's bounds, and 14.9.39.3 SR2 confines identifier-2 to 'a data item of class index' (cite.py PASS), whose content in this data model IS a long occurrence number (DATA_MODEL_DESIGN D3). A long is inside the documented range by construction, so arm a has no violating input and the rule holds VACUOUSLY for this carrier - which is a property of the choice recorded in CONFORMANCE.md section 7 row DOC-A.1-128, not an accident. It is nonetheless enforced STRUCTURALLY rather than argued: the sender goes through the same CobolIndex.TryAmount landing every Format-1 sender goes through, so if the index carrier ever widens past the range the test is already written and in the path. SetIndexAmountLandingDriftTests.EveryCallerOfTheIndexStore_LandsTheValueFirst holds that true for the next caller, and the 2002 golden proves the range raise is real at the edition where the mechanism arrives.

[folded GR-14.9.39.4-L2.3 = §14.9.39.4 2) a) 3.: CONFORMS]
kb/Work/PB459.md LANDED. FORMAT 1 GR2 a) 3 (index-name-2) plus the GR2 b)/GR2 c) tails. Arms a (same table - content placed unchanged), c (different table - the corresponding occurrence number) and the GR2 c) numeric-receiver tail were already measured correct and are unchanged: under the 3.5 occurrence-number identity a and c are the SAME machine operation, which is why the missing association went unnoticed for so long. Arm b, the cross-table range consequent, is now closed on the same derivation as -L2.2: the limit is the implementor index range (13.18.38.4 GR2), index-name-2's content is a long occurrence number (DATA_MODEL_DESIGN D3, documented as CONFORMANCE.md section 7 DOC-A.1-128), so no index-name-2 value can be outside it and the arm holds vacuously for this carrier - while the sender still travels the CobolIndex.TryAmount landing, so the test exists in the path rather than resting on the argument. The cross-table SET itself is LEGAL and is pinned as a control by the negative golden, which diagnoses only the cross-table SUBSCRIPT (8.4.2.3.3 SR4, COBOL1961) and must leave 'SET IX1 TO IX2' alone.
